design_detail: Open-label, fixed-order pharmacokinetic study in 15 healthy men with recreational MDMA experience who were all extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers, each acting as his own control. Session 1 (control): dextromethorphan 30 mg with caffeine 100 mg. Session 2 (at least 3 days later): MDMA 1.5 mg/kg by mouth (75 to 100 mg), then caffeine at 4 hours and repeated 30 mg doses of dextromethorphan from 4 hours onward. CYP2D6 activity was read from plasma dextromethorphan and its metabolites and from the urinary dextromethorphan to dextrorphan ratio (the metabolic ratio), and a recovery half-life was fitted to each man's ratio over 7 to 10 days. A pilot of 3 men used one dextromethorphan schedule, 12 men a second schedule (changed because the ratio had not recovered by 168 hours), and the two were pooled. There was no placebo session and no randomization or counterbalancing: the control session always came first, because the enzyme effect of MDMA lasts for days.
can_establish: Whether, in 15 healthy men with normal CYP2D6 activity, a single dose of 1.5 mg/kg MDMA is followed by a large fall in the enzyme's activity, measured with a probe drug (dextromethorphan exposure about 9 to 10 times higher, its CYP2D6 product about 90% lower, urinary ratio from about 0.006 to 0.43), that has not fully reversed after 10 days, and a rough size of the recovery half-life (about 47 hours from a one-phase fit).
cannot_establish: That the early change is mechanism-based inactivation rather than competition from the MDMA still in the blood (the first probe dose came 4 hours after MDMA, near MDMA's peak, and MDMA is itself a CYP2D6 substrate); how long inhibition lasts (a one-phase fit gives 46.6 hours, a two-phase fit 103 hours with a standard deviation of 70, and activity was not at baseline on day 10); what happens to MDMA blood levels after a second MDMA dose, or to any medicine other than dextromethorphan (not measured); anything in women, in slow, intermediate or ultrarapid metabolizers, at other MDMA doses, or in people who use MDMA often (none was studied); toxicity of any kind.

sample.recruitment: Men recruited by word of mouth; self-reported recreational MDMA use on at least 5 occasions and twice in the previous year (Materials and Methods, Subjects, 2nd paragraph). Interviewed by a physician, examined, laboratory tests, urinalysis and 12-lead ECG; interviewed by a psychiatrist (PRISM for DSM-IV). Approved by the local ethics board (CEIC-IMAS) and authorized by the Spanish Medicines Agency (AEM n. 04-0013); written consent; paid for taking part.
sample.inclusion_exclusion: Extensive-metabolizer phenotype by dextromethorphan was required; excluded: history of or current major psychiatric disorder (schizophrenia, psychosis, major affective disorder), abuse or dependence other than nicotine, adverse medical or psychiatric reactions to MDMA, regular medication in the previous month (single symptomatic doses accepted up to the week before). Asked to avoid drugs of abuse for 2 weeks before and during the study (urine screen before each session) and to follow a xanthine-free diet for 48 hours.
sample.demographics: All men; mean age 26 years (19 to 33), weight 69.6 kg (54.2 to 91.2), height 181 cm (171 to 196); on average 26 previous MDMA experiences (range 6 to 100); all but 4 were current smokers; all had used other psychostimulants, cannabis or hallucinogens. CYP2D6 genotypes (Subjects, 3rd paragraph): *1/*1 (1 man), *1/*2 (5), *1/*4 (2), *2/*4 (1), *1/*5 (1), *1/*9 (1), *1/*10 (1), *9/*10 (1), *1/*17 (1), *2/*41 (1), so no man carried two null alleles; 4 carried one (*4 or *5) and several carried reduced-function alleles.
sample.attrition: None reported; all 15 contribute to Table 1. The number of men at each urine time point is not stated: the 10-day point (240 to 248 hours) can come only from the 12 men of the final phase, and the 3 pilot men had no sample after 176 hours.
sample.selection_effects: Men only, young, healthy, experienced with MDMA, selected for normal enzyme activity at baseline (mean baseline metabolic ratio 0.0061, SD 0.0056) and for having no adverse reaction to MDMA before; volunteers took one dose in a hospital laboratory. Results therefore describe men like these.

exposure.measurement: MDMA given in the laboratory and measured in plasma (GC-MS, method of Pizarro et al., 2002): peak 194.3 ng/mL (SD 30.9) at 2.0 hours (SD 1.0), area under the curve to 25 hours 1939.7 (SD 484.7) (printed with the unit mg/mL x h, which cannot be right; probably ng/mL x h), mean residence time 13.3 hours (SD 2.3). The probe drug dextromethorphan was measured in plasma and urine by HPLC with stated limits of detection and precision (about 9 to 15%).
exposure.dose_frequency_duration_route: Study conditions only: a single oral MDMA dose of 1.5 mg/kg (minimum 75 mg, maximum 100 mg), described as the amount in a single ecstasy pill; probe doses of dextromethorphan 30 mg by mouth at 0 hours in session 1 and at 4, 24, 48 (pilot) or 72 (final), 96, 168 and 240 hours (final) in session 2; caffeine 100 mg.
exposure.polysubstance: No drug other than the probes (dextromethorphan, caffeine) and MDMA; the men were asked to avoid drugs of abuse for 2 weeks before and during the study and were screened by rapid urine test before each session. Tobacco smoking was not permitted for 6 hours after dosing.
exposure.abstinence_at_testing: Two weeks by request (not verified beyond the urine screen at the start of each session); overnight fast; xanthine-free diet for 48 hours; light meal 6 hours after dosing.

comparison.controls: Each man's own control session with dextromethorphan and caffeine alone (session 1), at least 3 days before the MDMA session. There was no placebo MDMA session.
comparison.matching: Within person, so no matching; the control session always came first (no randomization or counterbalancing).
comparison.unmeasured_premorbid: Genotype is listed for all 15 men; urine pH and creatinine were measured and did not correlate with the metabolic ratio in session 1 (r=0.049 and r=0.214), in a homogeneous sample on similar diets; whether anything else changed between sessions (smoking, diet, time of year) is not described.
comparison.controls_other_drug_use: Not described beyond the urine screen.

outcomes.instruments: Plasma dextromethorphan (DEX), dextrorphan (DOR), 3-methoxymorphinan (MM) and 3-hydroxymorphinan (HM) at up to 12 times over 25 hours; urinary DEX/DOR metabolic ratio (MR) in timed collections from 0 to 248 hours; plasma caffeine and paraxanthine (as a CYP1A2 marker; described as unaffected, not shown); recovery half-life of CYP2D6 from a mono-exponential fit to each man's fold change in MR.
outcomes.validity_norms: The urinary ratio is a standard probe of CYP2D6 activity; the poor-metabolizer antimode of 0.3 comes from a 1985 study cited by the authors. The ratio is sensitive to urine pH and renal clearance, which the authors checked at baseline only.
outcomes.operationalization: Activity change = the fold change of each man's MR after MDMA against his own control MR, fitted over time (weighted by the SD of the MR in each collection period), giving a half-life = ln 2 / Kcyp; corrected half-lives subtract MDMA's mean residence time; a two-phase curve was also fitted because the one-phase fit was thought to underestimate recovery.
outcomes.multiplicity_correction: None; paired Student t tests for peak and area (P<0.05) and the Wilcoxon test for time to peak; the main changes are large against their standard deviations.
outcomes.assessor_blinding: Open design, justified by the authors by the objective outcomes; blinding of the laboratory analysts is not described.

analysis.effect_sizes: Table 1 (n=15; mean and SD; all P<0.05 by paired t test unless noted): dextromethorphan peak 3.5 (3.6) to 29.7 (18.5) ng/mL and area over 8 hours 15.7 (5.2) to 149.1 (75.6) ng/mL x h, half-life 1.7 (0.1) to 9.0 (5.6) h; dextrorphan peak 464.6 (182.6) to 31.9 (12.6) and area 1877.1 (676.2) to 179.1 (77.6), half-life 2.5 (0.6) to 10.9 (5.7) h; 3-hydroxymorphinan peak 164.1 (58.0) to 16.6 (5.8) and area 764.2 (232.2) to 97.5 (38.0); 3-methoxymorphinan peak 2.7 (2.0) to 6.3 (5.1) and area 16.8 (5.3) to 28.8 (24.2), not significant. Editors' ratios of the printed means: dextromethorphan peak 8.5-fold and area 9.5-fold; dextrorphan peak 93% and area 90% lower. Urinary ratio 0.0061 (SD 0.0056) to 0.4322 (SD 0.2848): the ratio of the two means is 71-fold (the paper says almost 100-fold), and 67% of the men (10 of 15, editors' count) were above the poor-metabolizer antimode of 0.3 after MDMA (collection period not stated). The ratio correlated with the peak DEX/DOR ratio (r=0.594, P=0.002). Recovery: Kcyp 0.016 (SD 0.005) per hour (printed without the per), half-life 46.6 hours (SD 11.8), r2=0.791; corrected for MDMA residence time 37.4 (SD 11.6) hours; a two-phase fit gave 103.0 (SD 70.3) hours, corrected 93.7 (SD 70.4); the ratio had not recovered fully at 10 days (Discussion).
analysis.preregistration_detail: A trial authorized by the Spanish Medicines Agency (AEM n. 04-0013); no registry entry is mentioned.
analysis.selective_reporting: Caffeine and paraxanthine results are described as unaffected with no data shown; MDMA's effects and adverse events are summarized in two sentences; the number of men at each later time point is not given; the probe-dose schedule was changed after the first 3 men and the two groups pooled; plasma values below the assay limit were replaced by the limit (Table 1 title), which affects the baseline dextromethorphan values (mean peak 3.5 ng/mL against a limit of 1.5).
analysis.power: No sample-size reasoning; 15 men; the half-life is reported as a mean and SD only.

interpretation_gap.results_show: After 1.5 mg/kg MDMA, 15 men had about 9 to 10 times the plasma exposure to dextromethorphan and about 90% less of its CYP2D6 product; the urinary ratio rose from about 0.006 to 0.43 on average, with 10 of 15 men above the poor-metabolizer cut-off, and had not returned fully to baseline after 10 days. A one-phase model gave a recovery half-life of 47 hours (about 37 hours after the correction); a two-phase model gave about 100 hours with a standard deviation of 70. All probe doses came 4 hours or later after MDMA, so the first hours cannot be separated from competition for the enzyme by MDMA itself.
interpretation_gap.claimed: The abstract says CYP2D6 activity 'recovered after 10 days' (the Discussion says the ratio had not recovered fully at 10 days), that the ratio rose 'almost 100-fold' (71-fold by the printed means) and that people who use MDMA 'must be warned' of the consequences. The Discussion says the risk of acute toxicity with repeated doses and binges is 'drastically increased', that a second dose up to a week later would give higher plasma levels and 'higher risk of acute toxicity', and that people who use MDMA often may have 'permanently compromised' CYP2D6 activity. No second MDMA dose, no MDMA level after a second dose, no toxicity outcome and no person who uses MDMA often was studied, so these are inferences from a probe drug.

timeline.event: Same group: non-linear MDMA kinetics in men, which the authors there attributed either to saturation or to inactivation of CYP2D6
Same group: a second 100 mg dose 24 hours after the first raised MDMA exposure by 77% (cited here as in vivo evidence that MDMA inhibits its own metabolism)
Same group: 3 days of paroxetine before MDMA raised MDMA peak by 16% and exposure by 22%

Narrative review by the same group, which uses this study for the speed of recovery and for a statement of inhibition 'within 2 hours' that this study could not show (the first probe dose was at 4 hours)

Independent group: 7 people with no CYP2D6 function had a peak MDMA level 15% above people with normal function, in the first 3 hours only, which the authors read as MDMA blocking the enzyme in everyone

replication.where_it_stands: No second probe-drug study of MDMA's effect on CYP2D6 has been read. The direction (MDMA lowers CYP2D6 activity in people) is supported indirectly by other controlled studies, mostly from the same group, and by an independent pooled genotype analysis; the size and duration of the effect rest on these 15 men, and the duration is uncertain (one-phase 47 hours, two-phase 103 hours, not back to baseline at 10 days).

funding.funder: NIH grant 1 R01 DA017987; Generalitat de Catalunya grant 2005SGR00032; Spanish Network on Addiction Disorders (FIS-RTA RD06/0001/1009) (Acknowledgments footnote); MDMA supplied by the Spanish Ministry of Health.
funding.declared_conflicts: The authors state they have no conflicts of interest to disclose (Author Disclosure Information).
funding.affiliations_note: Most authors belong to the Barcelona group (IMIM-Hospital del Mar) that also wrote the 2000 non-linearity paper, the 2004 repeated-dose study, the 2007 paroxetine study and the 2012 review, so these are not independent of each other. Two authors are at the University of Sheffield and one at Simcyp Limited, a pharmacokinetic simulation company; the paper cites a model of MDMA kinetics from the Sheffield and Simcyp authors (Yang et al., 2006).

what_would_settle_it: A randomized, blinded crossover in people of known CYP2D6 genotype who take MDMA or placebo and then a CYP2D6 probe (dextromethorphan or another) at several times from 1 hour to 14 days, with MDMA concentrations measured so that competition and inactivation can be told apart, in women and men and at more than one dose; and a design that gives a second MDMA dose, or a medicine cleared by CYP2D6, at set intervals after the first and measures its levels and effects.

domains.note: Fixed order: the control session was always first and MDMA second. The authors had to do it this way, because the enzyme effect lasts for days, but the design cannot separate MDMA from order or time.

Control and MDMA sessions were at least 3 days apart and nothing was done to check that the control values were stable; the probe schedules and collection windows differ between the control and MDMA sessions and between the pilot and final phases.

Open design, with objective outcomes; the dextromethorphan schedule was changed after the first 3 men; abstinence from other drugs rests on the men's word and a urine screen at the start of each session.
All 15 men are in Table 1, but the number at each urine time point is not given and the 10-day point can come only from 12; plasma values below the assay limit were replaced by the limit.

Chromatographic assays with stated limits and precision (about 9 to 15%) and a selectivity check; the urinary ratio can be moved by urine pH and renal function, which were checked at baseline and not at later times.

No registration; the abstract overstates the recovery ('recovered after 10 days') and the size of the ratio change ('almost 100-fold') against the paper's own Discussion and printed means; some results (caffeine, paraxanthine, MDMA effects) are described but not shown.

risk_of_bias.reasoning: The outcomes are objective and the changes are large against their spread, but every comparison is the same men's own control session taken first, without a placebo or randomization, and the first probe dose came when MDMA itself was at its peak concentration, so competition for the enzyme cannot be separated from lasting inactivation in the early hours. The source can be cited for a large, long-lasting fall in the probe-drug measure of CYP2D6 activity after a single 1.5 mg/kg dose in 15 healthy men with normal baseline activity, with the later urine collections (from 24 hours) as the stronger evidence for inactivation; it cannot be cited for the length of recovery as a single number, for what happens to MDMA levels after a second dose, for toxicity, or for people who use MDMA often.

key_findings.finding: Fifteen healthy men (mean age 26, range 19 to 33; on average 26 previous MDMA experiences) who were extensive CYP2D6 metabolizers at screening, recruited by word of mouth and paid; genotypes: 1 *1/*1, 5 *1/*2, 2 *1/*4, 1 *2/*4, 1 *1/*5, 1 *1/*9, 1 *1/*10, 1 *9/*10, 1 *1/*17, 1 *2/*41. No man had two null alleles.
key_findings.locator: Materials and Methods > Subjects, 2nd paragraph (eligibility, 15 men, demographics) and 3rd paragraph (genotypes and their metabolic ratios)

key_findings.finding: Open, fixed-order design: session 1 (control, dextromethorphan 30 mg with caffeine 100 mg) then at least 3 days later session 2 (MDMA 1.5 mg/kg, 75 to 100 mg, then caffeine at 4 hours and 30 mg dextromethorphan at 4, 24, 48, 72, 96 and 168 hours in the 3-man pilot); the schedule was changed to 4, 24, 72, 96, 168 and 240 hours for the other 12 men because the ratio had not recovered by 168 hours; results pooled. No placebo MDMA session.
key_findings.locator: Materials and Methods > Drugs, 1st paragraph; Study Design, 1st to 4th paragraphs (the 4th, on the changed intervals, is on p. 527)

key_findings.finding: Plasma probe drug after MDMA against the control session (Table 1, n=15): dextromethorphan peak 3.5 to 29.7 ng/mL (SDs 3.6 and 18.5) and area over 8 hours 15.7 to 149.1; dextrorphan peak 464.6 to 31.9 and area 1877.1 to 179.1; 3-hydroxymorphinan peak 164.1 to 16.6 and area 764.2 to 97.5 (all P<0.05); 3-methoxymorphinan not significantly changed; dextromethorphan half-life 1.7 to 9.0 hours.
key_findings.locator: Table 1 (p. 527); Results > Plasma Concentrations of DEX, DOR, MM, HM, and MDMA Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamic Effects, 1st paragraph (p. 528)

key_findings.finding: MDMA kinetics in these men: peak 194.3 ng/mL (SD 30.9) at 2.0 hours (SD 1.0), mean residence time 13.3 hours (SD 2.3); the dose produced the usual laboratory effects (higher blood pressure and heart rate, wider pupils, well-being, euphoria) and no adverse effects were noted.

Urinary dextromethorphan to dextrorphan ratio rose from 0.0061 (SD 0.0056) to 0.4322 (SD 0.2848), described as almost 100-fold (the ratio of the printed means is 71-fold); 67% of the men were above the 0.3 poor-metabolizer antimode after MDMA (10 of 15 by the editors' count; the collection period is not stated); no correlation of the ratio with urine pH (r=0.049) or creatinine (r=0.214) at baseline.
key_findings.locator: Results > Urinary DEX/DOR MR and CYP2D6 Recovery Half-Life, 1st paragraph

key_findings.finding: Recovery of CYP2D6 activity fitted with one exponential curve: rate constant 0.016 (SD 0.005) per hour, recovery half-life 46.6 hours (SD 11.8), r2=0.791 (Figure 2).
key_findings.locator: Results > Urinary DEX/DOR MR and CYP2D6 Recovery Half-Life, 2nd paragraph; Figure 2 (p. 528)

key_findings.finding: Discussion: the ratio had not recovered fully to baseline at 10 days; the half-life corrected for MDMA's own residence time is 37.4 hours (SD 11.6), and the authors think it underestimates recovery because activity had not recovered even at 10 days; a two-phase fit gives 103.0 hours (SD 70.3), corrected 93.7 (SD 70.4), though variability and few time points 'question the validity of the biphasic model'.
key_findings.locator: Discussion, 1st paragraph (p. 528, 'not recovered fully ... at 10 days'); 3rd paragraph (p. 529, half-life estimates)

key_findings.finding: The authors compare the effect with paroxetine, also a mechanism-based inhibitor: a single recreational dose of MDMA is said to inhibit CYP2D6 rapidly and completely whereas several prescription doses of paroxetine are needed for similar inhibition, and they point to MDMA phenocopying poor metabolizers as the reason acute toxicity has not been related to genotype.

Statements in the Discussion that go beyond the data: a dose greater than 50 mg would almost completely inactivate CYP2D6 in the liver (from a model, ref. 17); risk of acute toxicity with repeated doses and binges 'drastically increased'; a second dose up to a week later would give higher plasma concentrations and higher risk of acute toxicity; people who use MDMA often may have permanently compromised CYP2D6 activity; people taking an SSRI with multiple MDMA doses should know that metabolism of both is compromised; SSRIs such as citalopram and paroxetine block MDMA's positive effects (refs. 41, 42); the only fatal interaction reported to date was with ritonavir (ref. 40).

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract says CYP2D6 activity 'recovered after 10 days with a recovery half-life of 46.6 hours'; the Discussion says the ratio 'had not recovered fully' at 10 days and that activity 'has not recovered fully even after 10 days'.
reporting_issues.consequence: The abstract overstates recovery. The paper's data support only that the ratio was still above baseline at 10 days; the half-life depends on the model (46.6 hours one-phase, 103 hours two-phase).

reporting_issues.issue: The abstract and Results say the metabolic ratio rose 'almost 100-fold' from 0.0061 to 0.4322; the ratio of those two means is 71-fold, and the average of the individual fold changes (which could be larger) is not given.
reporting_issues.consequence: Use the printed means (0.006 to 0.43) rather than a fold figure.

reporting_issues.issue: '67% of the subjects' had a ratio above the 0.3 poor-metabolizer antimode after MDMA, without saying in which urine collection period; with 15 men the share is 10 men, and 5 stayed below the cut-off.
reporting_issues.consequence: The share of men who reached poor-metabolizer values depends on the sampling time, and a third did not reach them; the paper does not support saying that everyone became a poor metabolizer.

reporting_issues.issue: The first probe dose after MDMA was given 4 hours after it, when plasma MDMA was near its peak (mean peak 194 ng/mL at 2 hours), and MDMA is itself a CYP2D6 substrate. The early rise in probe-drug exposure therefore mixes competition for the enzyme with inactivation of it.
reporting_issues.consequence: The study does not show inhibition 'within 2 hours' (as the 2012 review of the same group states); the later collections (24 hours onward) are the evidence for lasting inactivation.

reporting_issues.issue: Units are misprinted: MDMA area under the curve '1939.7 +/- 484.7 mg/mL x h' (the value fits ng/mL x h) and Kcyp '0.016 +/- 0.005 hours' (it is a rate per hour; ln 2 / 0.016 = 43 hours is consistent with the stated half-life).
reporting_issues.consequence: Printed units cannot be taken literally; the values are consistent with the rest of the paper.

reporting_issues.issue: The dextromethorphan schedule was changed after the first 3 men because the ratio had not recovered by 168 hours; the pilot and final phases differ in dosing times and urine windows and were pooled. The 10-day point comes from 12 men and the number at each time point is not stated; plasma values below the limit of detection were replaced by the limit (Table 1 title).
reporting_issues.consequence: The pooled half-life mixes two schedules and a changing number of men; the baseline dextromethorphan values (peak 3.5 ng/mL, limit 1.5) are partly the assay limit, so the roughly 9-fold rise is approximate.

reporting_issues.issue: The Discussion's risk statements (acute toxicity 'drastically increased' by repeated doses or binges; a second dose a week later would give higher levels and higher risk of acute toxicity; people who use MDMA often may have permanently compromised activity) are not tested here: no second MDMA dose, no MDMA level after one, no toxicity outcome and no person who uses MDMA often was studied, and the data show recovery under way by 10 days.
reporting_issues.consequence: Cite the paper for a probe-drug fall that lasts for days after one dose; the statements about toxicity and people who use MDMA often are the authors' inference.

reporting_issues.issue: The statement that people who use MDMA 'may take common SSRIs to modify the effects of MDMA' is referenced (ref. 43) to a rat study of fluoxetine and MDMA nerve damage, which does not show what people do.
reporting_issues.consequence: No evidence of people taking SSRIs to change MDMA's effects comes from this paper; the 2007 paroxetine paper cites internet forums for it.

reporting_issues.issue: 3-methoxymorphinan means roughly doubled (peak 2.7 to 6.3; area 16.8 to 28.8) and the text says they were 'not changed by MDMA'; the SDs were as large as the means.
reporting_issues.consequence: Not significant is not the same as unchanged; the sample is too small to say.

verification.source_read: PDF OMathuna_2008_MDMACYP2D6Inhibition.pdf (7 pages, pp. 525-531), text extracted once with pdftotext; Table 1 and Figures 1 and 2 checked on rendered pages 3 and 4. Supplementary material: none.
